rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess/predict-then-reveal demo instruction anywhere in the file; this is a reference supplementary, not a live-demo lecture/exercise beat.

Checked all six sub-items, none fire as violations. 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction — absent (only single, non-triple negations, e.g. line 7 'is not thrift'). Anaphora/epistrophe triples — the one candidate, line 13 'Some people count tokens per task. Some watch cache-hit-rate. Some track cost per pull request,' has a third leg carrying genuinely new concrete content (a distinct metric, not filler), satisfying rule 7's own escape clause. Self-grading superlatives — 'the cheapest quality upgrade there is' (line 41) and 'the cheapest line on the bill' (line 35) grade the PRACTICE/technique, not the training's own usefulness (the banned shape is self-praise of 'the training'/'the exercise') — not flagged. Number+own-retraction — the 15x multi-agent figure (chunk 5, line 79) and the 90%-caching figure (chunk 4, line 57) both pair a number with an immediate caveat, but both are maintainer-attested in the file's own source-verification block as the deliberate teaching shape (15x framed as 'a research-style ceiling, not a coding default'; 90% 'presented AS folklore on purpose, not asserted') — accept-with-note, no edit. Abstraction-noun stacks — absent (concrete nouns throughout: 'the files Claude didn't load' register, not '-ity'/compound-abstraction stacks). Verb triplets with an empty leg — absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 5 "Drivers of inefficient context" (lines 63-80): carries 7 bolded spans. 5 are legitimate one-handle-per-driver names ('The codebase the agent reads.', 'Thin memory, both directions.', 'The tool and MCP surface.', 'Cache invalidation.', 'Fanning out too wide.') and fit the consolidation-slide allowance ('a law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law'). But 2 more are bolded FULL SENTENCES functioning as category dividers, not named-law handles: line 67 "**Durable, so engineer around these.**" and line 73 "**Loud but shrinking, so check before you chase.**" (the second runs ~8 words) — both breach 'Bold the handle (≲ 5 words, a sub-span), never a whole lead sentence' and push the chunk past the one-handle-per-law reading to 7 bolds on a single slide. (Chunk 3's 5-item 'moves that hold up' list, by contrast, bolds only the 5 short move-names and no category label — clean, not flagged.)
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Un-bold the two category-transition sentences at lines 67 and 73 (or shorten each to a short label sub-span, e.g. bold just 'Durable' / 'Loud but shrinking'); keep bold only on the 5 driver-name handles.
